meta.title: Reading and influences
meta.note: The order of these links changes from time to time. That is intentional. Learning is rarely linear, and neither is change.

tiers.label: Start here
tiers.microCopy: A way in, not a conclusion.

items.name: Harvard Business Review
items.annotation: A shared reference point for contemporary leadership and organisational debate, useful precisely because it reflects the mainstream as well as its limits.

items.name: MIT Sloan Management Review
items.annotation: Consistently stronger than most management outlets on digital transformation, organisational learning, and the gap between technology and outcomes.

items.name: Government Digital Service – Service Manual
items.annotation: Practical, opinionated guidance grounded in real public-sector delivery rather than theory alone.

items.name: Institute for Government
items.annotation: Clear analysis of how government actually works, including constraints, incentives, and institutional reality.

tiers.label: Go deeper
tiers.microCopy: When the simple explanations stop working.

items.name: Oxford Review
items.annotation: Evidence-based management writing that actively challenges intuition, fads, and consultant-friendly simplifications.

items.name: Academy of Management Perspectives
items.annotation: Translational research that explains why sensible change efforts fail once they meet real organisations.

items.name: Behavioural Insights Team
items.annotation: Applied behavioural science with a strong track record in public services, policy, and organisational change.

items.name: OECD – Observatory of Public Sector Innovation
items.annotation: International perspectives on public-sector innovation that balance ambition with evidence and feasibility.

tiers.label: Challenge your assumptions
tiers.microCopy: This may change how you see the problem.

items.name: Evidence-Based Change (Fielding Graduate University)
items.annotation: Work rooted in Argyris and Schön, focused on inquiry, defensive routines, and double-loop learning.

items.name: Santa Fe Institute
items.annotation: Complexity science applied to systems and organisations, challenging linear planning and control assumptions.

items.name: AI Now Institute
items.annotation: Critical research on AI, power, governance, and social consequences that resists techno-neutral narratives.

items.name: Centre for the Edge
items.annotation: Thought-provoking work on learning, unlearning, and institutional adaptation under accelerating change.

items.name: London Review of Books
items.annotation: Long-form essays that reward slow reading and sharpen how arguments are constructed and challenged.

items.name: The New York Review of Books
items.annotation: Critical essays that connect politics, culture, history, and power with intellectual seriousness.

items.name: BFI – Sight and Sound
items.annotation: Writing on cinema as cultural and political artefact, not just entertainment.

items.name: Aeon
items.annotation: Accessible but serious essays on philosophy, psychology, systems, and how we make meaning.
